title: Fix a Scatter-Gather Chat Read
description: A chat service shards its messages table by hash(message_id) across 16 shards. The most frequent query, "latest 50 messages in a conversation," must query all 16 shards, and its p99 latency tracks the slowest shard. What change best fixes this?

options.text: Add more shards so each one holds fewer messages.
options.explanation: The query still fans out to every shard, and with more shards the chance that one is slow rises, so tail latency gets worse.

options.text: Repartition by conversation_id with message time as the sort key, adding a time bucket for very large conversations.
options.explanation: The dominant query then names its partition key and reads one shard in order. The time bucket keeps any single conversation from growing an unbounded partition.

options.text: Range-partition by created_at so recent messages sit together.
options.explanation: Every new message would land on the newest range, creating a write hot spot, and one conversation still spans many writers.

options.text: Keep message_id partitioning and add a global secondary index on conversation_id.
options.explanation: This can work, but it doubles writes, global indexes typically lag, and the main access pattern still depends on a secondary structure. The primary key should serve the hottest query.
